questions.prompt: When are dual turns permitted at an intersection?
questions.explanation: Two lanes may turn at the same time only where pavement markings or signs show that dual turns are allowed. Key words: "dual turns".

choices.text: Only when turning from a one-way road onto a one-way road
Any time there are at least 2 lanes on the road being entered
Only when indicated by pavement markings or traffic control signs
Only when the road has 6 or more lanes

questions.prompt: Unless otherwise permitted, what lane must a driver be in to turn left from a one-way road?
questions.explanation: To turn left from a one-way road, start from the lane nearest the left curb, unless signs or pavement markings allow another lane.

choices.text: The centre lane
The lane closest to the right curb
The left lane nearest the left curb
The lane to the right of centre

questions.prompt: At a stop sign, a driver must:
questions.explanation: Stop before the stop line or the marked crosswalk. If there is neither, stop before entering the intersection at a point where you can see approaching traffic.

choices.text: Stop in a position where the visibility is the greatest
Stop 10 metres before a marked crosswalk or stop line
Stop in the marked crosswalk or on the stop line
Stop before entering a marked crosswalk or crossing a stop line

questions.explanation: An uncontrolled intersection has no traffic lights or signs. Slow down, be ready to stop, and yield to the vehicle on your right.

choices.text: Has a flashing yellow light for one direction of traffic and a flashing red light for the other direction of traffic
Has traffic signs but no traffic control signal lights
Has no traffic control signal lights or traffic signs
Has Yield signs but no Stop signs

questions.prompt: U-turns in urban areas are not permitted at:
questions.explanation: In urban areas, U-turns are not allowed at intersections controlled by traffic lights unless a sign allows them. They are also not allowed between intersections or at alleys. Key words: "urban areas", "not".

choices.text: An intersection with marked traffic lanes
Roads with a landscaped median
An intersection controlled by a traffic control signal
An intersection controlled by Stop signs

questions.prompt: A driver attempting to turn left at a steady green traffic light:
questions.explanation: A steady green light does not give a left-turning driver the right-of-way. Yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians, and turn only when it is safe.

choices.text: Has the right-of-way over oncoming traffic
Must stop before the pedestrian crosswalk line, then proceed
Has the right-of-way over pedestrians
Must not cross the path of an approaching vehicle unless it is safe

questions.prompt: When turning left from a two-way road onto a one-way road, what lane should the vehicle enter?
questions.explanation: When turning left onto a one-way road, enter the lane nearest the left curb. Key words: "onto a one-way road", "left side".

choices.text: The lane immediately to the right of centre
The lane nearest the curb on the left side of the one-way road
The centre lane of the one-way road
The right lane of the one-way road

questions.prompt: A driver entering a traffic circle:
questions.explanation: Vehicles already in a traffic circle have the right-of-way. When entering, yield to them and wait for a safe gap. Key words: "entering".

choices.text: Must yield to traffic on the right
Must yield to vehicles in the traffic circle
Has the right-of-way

questions.prompt: A vehicle exiting a parking lot onto a roadway:
questions.explanation: When leaving a parking lot, alley or driveway, come to a complete stop before the sidewalk area, then yield to pedestrians and to traffic on the road.

choices.text: Must stop only if there is a Stop sign
Is not required to stop
Must stop before crossing the sidewalk only if there are pedestrians present
Must come to a complete stop

questions.prompt: When approaching a Yield sign, you must:
questions.explanation: At a yield sign, slow down and be ready to stop. Give the right-of-way to traffic that does not face the sign and to all pedestrians, and go only when it is safe.

choices.text: Yield the right-of-way to traffic not facing the sign and all pedestrians in the intersection
Always sound the horn to warn other traffic within the intersection
Expect all other vehicles to yield the right-of-way to you
Come to a stop and proceed after looking to the right and left

questions.prompt: When two vehicles approach an uncontrolled "T" intersection at right angles to each other at approximately the same time:
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection, including a "T" intersection, the vehicle on the left yields to the vehicle on the right. Key words: "left".

choices.text: The vehicle on the left must yield the right-of-way
The vehicle on the left has the right-of-way
The vehicle going straight through always has the right-of-way
Both vehicles must stop
